content.title: Review idea: Status filter dropdown shows raw status values instead of labels

content.content:
Review decision: APPROVE for implementation.

Verified against the code. packages/webapp/frontend/src/components/ui/select.tsx wraps @base-ui/react's Select.Value, which renders the RAW selected value by default and only shows a label when given a render-function child. In IssueFilters.tsx both the Status and Assignee filters render <SelectValue /> with no child, so the trigger shows the raw value. The defect is visible on the Status filter because its values ('closed', 'in-progress', 'todo') differ from their labels ('Closed', 'In Progress', 'Todo'); the Assignee filter is unaffected in practice because value == username == label.

The idea's root-cause analysis and suggested fix are correct and minimal.

Recommended implementation (single file, ~5 lines):
- In IssueFilters.tsx, give SelectValue a render child that maps the current value to its STATUS_OPTIONS label, e.g. build a const STATUS_LABEL: Record<string,string> from STATUS_OPTIONS and render <SelectValue>{(value) => STATUS_LABEL[value] ?? value}</SelectValue>. base-ui's Select.Value supports this function-as-child signature.
- Apply the same pattern to the Assignee trigger for consistency (optional; no visible change today).

Scope and impact: cosmetic only; filtering behavior is correct and unaffected. No library/CLI changes.

Suggested follow-up: create an implementation task for webapp-developer (fix + unit/component assertion that the trigger shows the label) and a validation task for webapp-validator (extend the URL-driven filtering E2E to assert the trigger text for /?status=closed is 'Closed', not 'closed'). Priority: low. I'm leaving planning/issue creation to the project-manager per the downstream 'Check review decision' gate.

Done. Reviewed idea mqgxk7rj2a, confirmed root cause in code, approved for implementation with concrete fix guidance. No code changes made (review gate only). Handing back to project-manager for the 'Check review decision' step.
